prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to eliminate chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Having read the eight openings, I move my first preference from B026 to B027. Five of eight members ranked targeted protein degradation in their top four, and the reason is scientific, not merely popular: a defined chemical mechanism (a bifunctional or glue molecule forces proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, ubiquitination follows, and the proteasome removes the protein) was shown in vitro, in cells and structurally, and then reproduced by many independent groups. The cereblon finding explains in molecular terms what thalidomide does, which gives the glue branch a mechanistic anchor and not just a clinical history. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, so the three names map onto the two founding branches without needing a fourth. As Secretary I would also note that this candidacy is comparatively easy to evaluate against the expert reports: the concept, the chemistry and the independent confirmation are all documented, and the field is broad enough that the reports can be written with confidence.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution and maturity. Credit is crowded: Sakamoto, Ito, Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures) and later contributors all have real claims, and a three-name limit leaves out people some will regard as essential. Whether PROTACs and molecular glues are one discovery or two distinct achievements is not settled, and a single citation may hide that. There is also no approved PROTAC drug yet, so the clinical validation is still maturing, and a committee that cares about durable interpretation could reasonably wait. Finally, I have not seen the expert reports in this round and am relying on the openings and memory.

responses.point: Heiner ranks B027 first but would credit Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, treating cereblon and molecular glues as a distinct discovery that would crowd the citation.
responses.response: I take the point that the glue branch is conceptually separate, but I would not drop Handa for Ciulli. Ciulli's VHL ligand work is a refinement of the PROTAC idea that Crews and Deshaies had already shown, while Handa's identification of cereblon explains a drug mechanism that was previously unexplained. In priority terms Handa is the more independent contribution. If the committee prefers a PROTAC-only prize, then Ciulli is defensible, but I would want the expert reports to say explicitly why the glue branch can be left out.

responses.point: Daniel ranks lipid nanoparticles first, arguing that rational ionizable-lipid design enabled siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines and that the impact is immediate and clinically proven.
responses.response: The clinical impact is not in doubt and I rate it as high as Daniel does. My difficulty is attribution and fit: his own opening admits that Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer all have strong claims, and Emma and Daniel name different trios from the same list, so six people compete for three places. Zou also placed it seventh. The three-laureate limit makes B062 a harder fit than B027, and I would like to understand the formulation history from the expert reports before supporting it.

responses.point: Emma ranks lipid nanoparticles first and phase separation second, emphasizing lipid self-assembly physical chemistry and the multivalency framework for condensates.
responses.response: I agree that condensates are a physically clear concept and I kept B050 as an alternative for that reason. My reservation is the one Emma herself raises: it is still contested which condensates are truly liquid and functional in cells, and the theory contributors Pappu and Mittag would be excluded by a trio of Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen. I think that is a stronger objection to a prize this year than the open questions around degraders, where the mechanism is already independently confirmed.

responses.point: Andrei ranks base editing first as a clean deaminase reaction turned into a general tool, with Liu as a single laureate, and notes the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the timing a judgement call.
responses.response: Base editing is chemically neat and I agree that Liu is the central figure, but I share Andrei's worry about the 2020 prize: the committee would be asked to separate base editing from a genome-editing story it has already honoured. Degraders are a less awkward fit because there is no earlier prize for the same modality. I would keep B038 in reserve for a later year rather than put it ahead of B027 now.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports treat PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues as one achievement or two, which determines whether Handa belongs in the same citation.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug should delay recognition.
Whether Ciulli or Sakamoto should replace a named laureate; I cannot resolve this from the openings alone.
My earlier first choice, B026 (Gray and Winkler), received no support from colleagues and I could not verify how the reports compare it with the electron-transfer work already honoured in 1992.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I note only that I am Secretary and a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, neither of which bears on any shortlisted candidate.
